newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU jobs summit must give public confidence-Juncker.
newsitem.headline: EU jobs summit must give public confidence-Juncker.

text.p: A special European Union jobs summit in November must bolster public confidence and not turn into a "media circus", Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Thursday.

"I would like this summit to create more confidence in public opinion that we can create (more) jobs in Europe," Juncker told a Luxembourg meeting of the European People's Party (EEP), a grouping of mainly Christian Democrat politicians.
Juncker is adamant that while the Luxembourg summit cannot produce miracles, it must do more than just rehash old ideas.
"I refuse to organise a media circus (on unemployment) in November which merely repeats things we have said before. We really must add something...," he said.

Juncker said a "deregulation summit calling for extreme liberalisation measures" should be avoided, adding that people already in employment should not be made to feel at risk. "All we have to do is call for more flexibility," he said.
Juncker, whose country took over the EU presidency on July 1, was given the task of organising a jobs summit by EU leaders meeting in Amsterdam last month.
There, employment was thrust to the top of the agenda when France agreed to an EU budget stability pact only in return for a resolution on jobs and growth.

The resolution reflected growing concern that in the austerity drive neeeded to get member states in shape for a single currency, the EU was losing sight of social issues. However it contained no commitment to extra spending on jobs schemes.
Juncker was particularly concerned that Europe's economic growth performance was lower than the United States and the Far East, which he said was "not normal".
Better coordination of economic policy was needed in Europe, he said, and an "economic forum" should act as a counterweight to the future central European bank.

He saw no conflict between a policy of more jobs and the budgetary constraint needed for economic and monetary union (EMU), though he agreed that financing employment schemes must not make extra demands on the European or national budgets.
"We need an 'employment pact' through the Union to commit everyone to jobs, including the social partners (employers and trade unions)," he said.
"We have to see what we can do to liberate public and private funds to the jobs market."
Juncker said setting specific, measurable targets, such as increasing the number of jobless people in vocational training could be useful here.
The European Investment Bank (EIB), the EU's lending arm, is also being asked to step up its efforts with more investment.
